newsitem.title: UK: Zinc consumers come out of woodwork on low price.
newsitem.headline: Zinc consumers come out of woodwork on low price.

text.p: Zinc consumers, after holding off for weeks, took advantage of Tuesday's crash in futures prices to book physical metal, European traders said.

Futures prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME) plummeted $300 a tonne on Tuesday on waves of speculative and stop-loss selling but managed a modest recovery, with cash metal ending the day at $1,554.
"They were coming in at the bottom of the market, between $1,500 and $1,550 cash. I booked substantial business there yesterday," one physical trader said.
Much of the activity was on an outright, fixed-price basis instead of using a formula or premium, traders added.
"People who cannot hedge or do not hedge will buy physical material at fixed prices, those were the ones who showed interest yesterday," one said.
Another said spot business was being done with Asian and Middle East markets who did not normally have term contracts and were interested in buying at an outright price.
Premiums were hard to pin down with substantial business done at outright prices, but traders quoted Special High Grade in Rotterdam in a wide range from $25 to $55 above LME cash.

"I would say more towards $55, physical zinc is still tight. You can see from the backwardation," one trader said. There was more agreement on CIS material in Rotterdam, which was seen at a $15/$20 discount.
One trader in continental Europe said he was still doing business on Wednesday morning even though prices ticked higher, but several others said buying interest dried up.
"A lot of people are either on holiday or going to stand back for as long as they possibly can. There certainly would be more interest if the price came off another $100/$150," he said.
Some consumers booked material up to the end of the year, traders said.
"A few people have come in and priced forward for the end of the year because compared to the cash price at the moment, October to December is looking quite attractive," a trader said.
Due to the backwardation, December LME futures were about $200 less than cash on Wednesday morning.
